concept.name: Visible-range volume profile
concept.definition: A volume profile computed over whatever bars are currently visible on the screen: the histogram and its POC, value area, and nodes automatically rebuild every time the user scrolls or zooms. It provides an always-current volume-at-price read of the displayed range without manual anchoring.
concept.intuition: The profile follows your eyes — zoom into a week and it profiles the week; zoom out to a year and it profiles the year.
concept.mechanics: The platform continuously recomputes the volume-by-price histogram over the visible bar range using lower-timeframe data; POC, value area, and node levels update dynamically as the visible window changes.
concept.failure_modes: Because the range shifts with zoom and scroll, levels are unstable — a POC can jump when one more day enters the view — and users can mistake viewport artifacts for market structure.
concept.misconceptions: VRVP levels are not objectively 'the' market levels; they describe exactly the window on screen, and comparing levels across different zoom states is incoherent.
concept.example: Zoomed to the last three months, the VRVP shows the POC at 4,450 and a thin LVN band at 4,520; the trader uses those levels for context, then zooms to the last week for finer intraday nodes.

citations.source: TradingView — Volume profile indicators: basic concepts (visible range volume profile type)
